history.caption: Validating specific premises exactly at the moment of commit prevents agents from executing stale, invalid decisions.
history.title: Agent-Premise-Commit-Gate

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical inspection gate on a textured brushed steel surface. An asymmetric off-centre composition with the mechanism positioned to the right, leaving generous negative space on the left. The assembly consists of a central matte polymer module held by a sequence of three precise interlocking inspection pins aligned in a rack rail. Hard clean edges, muted modern industrial palette of charcoal grey and brushed silver. One directional key light from the upper left throwing a long, distinct cast shadow. Generous negative space, no bare geometry, no molded or printed lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, watermarks, UI elements, human faces, hands, bare abstract cubes
rationale: Component assembly perfectly translates abstract software architecture into a tangible structural mechanism. A mechanical gate checking aligned pins embodies the commit-time premise check without relying on lazy software tropes.
subject: a modular mechanical inspection gate checking aligned verification pins
core_thesis: A long-running agent commits facts it read minutes ago, so the fix is to record the premises the decision used and recheck exactly those at commit.
core_conflict: Stale data writes vs. commit-time premise validation
